author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
habitat: 물이 얕게 고인 논, 강 하구, 갯벌
summary: 봄과 가을에 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새이다. 물이 얕게 고인 논, 강 하구, 갯벌에서 무리 지어 먹이를 찾으며, 갯지렁이와 갑각류 같은 여러 무척추동물을 먹고 농경지에서는 볍씨도 먹는다. 유라시아 대륙 중부에서 번식하고 아프리카, 유럽 남부, 인도, 동남아시아, 호주에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Black-tailed Godwit (Limosa limosa), adult male in breeding plumage as seen in flooded Korean rice fields in April and May: head, neck and upper breast rich rufous-chestnut, the crown finely streaked dark and a paler supercilium in front of the eye; mantle and scapulars spotted and barred black and rufous, mixed with some plain grey feathers; wing coverts mostly plain grey-brown; lower breast and flanks white crossed by black bars; belly and vent white. Bill very long and straight, pinkish-orange on the basal half and black towards the tip; dark eye; legs long and blackish.
art.pose: wading in a shallow flooded rice field, probing with its long bill
art.scene: Korean flooded rice paddies in spring with shallow standing water; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding plumage (April–May), side view standing: rufous-chestnut head, neck and upper breast, black-and-rufous spotted back, black-barred white flanks, white vent, very long straight bill pink-orange at the base with a black tip, long blackish legs
adult female breeding plumage, side view standing: larger, with a longer bill, paler and more washed-out rufous on head and breast, fewer bright feathers on the back
adult non-breeding plumage, side view standing: plain grey-brown upperparts and breast, white belly, short whitish supercilium, pink-based bill
in flight seen from above: bold white wing-bar along the whole wing, white rump and tail base, broad black band across the end of the tail, feet projecting beyond the tail
art.build: Large, tall, elegant wader, 36.5–38.5cm including the long bill, standing much taller than a pigeon on very long legs, with a long neck. Bill very long, about twice the head length, straight or barely upturned near the tip. Legs long, blackish, with much bare tibia. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a bold white wing-bar along the whole wing, a white rump and tail base, a broad black terminal tail band, and the feet projecting well beyond the tail. Females are larger, longer-billed and paler.
avoid: Do not paint a barred tail, no wing-bar or an upturned bill — those mark Bar-tailed Godwit.
Do not paint a downcurved bill like a curlew or Whimbrel; the bill is straight.
Do not paint rufous over the whole belly and vent; the lower underparts are white with black bars on the flanks.
Do not paint yellow, green or red legs; they are blackish.
